results.notes: rust-nostr 0.45 through its UniFFI Python bindings: relay I/O, parsing and verification run on tokio threads; each notification crosses the FFI (a NEW_EVENT plus a MESSAGE for every EVENT frame), id via Event.id().to_hex(). The stream handle_notifications wraps. notification_channel_size raised to 2x the workload (a broadcast channel drops what a slow consumer has not read). The EOSE only arrives as a MESSAGE notification, so the app calls RelayMessage.as_enum() (an FFI call) on every MESSAGE notification to spot it. Drops expired (NIP-40) events. New Client per run. Headline row because stream_events loses events with a Python consumer (see nostr-sdk-stream).

results.crypto: libsecp256k1 (C, via the Rust secp256k1 crate, inside the UniFFI .so)
results.notes: short-lived stream, ends at EOSE. When the Python consumer falls behind the relay (per-event FFI await ~60-120 us vs the Rust reader), the stream ends early, with no error item, after a few thousand events (reproduced with a 0.1 ms sleep per event: 2,558 of 29,548; under machine load without any sleep: 12,979 then 9,073). notification_channel_size does not change it, so this is presumably the relay's internal notification broadcast channel lagging. Diagnostic row.

pynostr verifies every EVENT before calling message_callback with the parsed JSON list: Event.from_dict drops the wire id and recomputes it, verify() checks the sig against that recomputed id (coincurve), and nothing compares it with the wire id. The harness does: it recomputes the id with pynostr's own Event.from_dict(...).id (a second hash: the callback gets the JSON, not pynostr's Event), drops a mismatch, and counts the wire id. RelayManager(timeout=0): the default 2 s timeout covers the whole read loop. Connects lazily inside run_sync: the connect is inside the timed part (~1 ms on loopback). Each frame is json.loads-ed three times by pynostr.

results.notes: same pipeline as pynostr-callback; the app drains the MessagePool's Event objects after run_sync returns at EOSE (the pool parses each frame again into an Event, id recomputed). The wire id is never compared with the recomputed one, and it is not reachable here: Event.from_dict drops it and the pool's EventMessage holds only that Event, so the id counted is pynostr's recomputed id.

results.websocket: websocket-client 1.9 WebSocketApp (pure Python, one thread per relay)
results.notes: jeffthibault/python-nostr 0.0.2 (Jan 2023, the PyPI `nostr` package, unmaintained). Relay._is_valid_message verifies every event (Event.verify recomputes the id and checks the sig against it, but never compares it with the wire id the Event keeps) and matches the filter, then the MessagePool parses the frame again. The harness compares the wire id with the library's own Event.compute_id(...) (a second hash: verify() returns only a bool) and counts the wire id. An exception in verify ("sig": "") is swallowed by websocket-client's callback wrapper, dropping that event. Bug: Event() turns created_at 0 into now (`created_at or int(time.time())`), so a valid event with created_at 0 fails verification and is dropped. The app reads the pool's queue from the main thread (5 ms poll when empty).

results.websocket: websocket-client 1.9 WebSocketApp (pure Python, one thread per relay)
results.notes: maintained fork of python-nostr (gitlab 1440000bytes/python-nostr, 2026); same `nostr` module name, so it is installed in its own overlay. Relay verifies every event (sig checked against the id computed from the fields) inside a try/except that rejects anything that raises, and matches the filter. The wire id is never compared and cannot be: Event has no id field (the id property recomputes it on every access, so the pool's dedup and the app's read hash again) and Relay builds the Event without the wire id, which the delivered EventMessage does not carry. add_relay sleeps 1 s (untimed); the REQ goes out from a queue-worker thread that polls every 0.1 s while disconnected and is left behind (daemon) after each run. App reads the pool's queue (5 ms poll when empty).

results.api: Client.run() + Client.subscribe(filters, eose_func=...): stored events handed over as a list at EOSE
results.notes: monstr's Client does not verify received events; the harness calls Event.is_valid() (sig against the id field) and checks the id with Event.serialize() + sha256. Client(eose_timeout=None): the default sends a fake EOSE after 10 s. Client.run() GETs the relay's NIP-11 document over HTTP before the websocket connect (no option turns it off; in the untimed setup).

fetch-all; query() polls for completion every 100 ms, so up to 0.1 s of each run is that sleep. Its timeout (Client(query_timeout=...) and query(timeout=...), default 10 s, raises QueryTimeoutException) is raised to the run timeout. Verification, eose_timeout and NIP-11 GET as monstr-subscribe.

aionostr does not verify received events; the harness calls Event.verify() (sig against an id it recomputes with json.dumps compact, ensure_ascii=False) and compares Event.compute_id(...) with the event's id field, which verify() never does: two hashes per event, as verify() keeps its id to itself. Bug: Event() turns created_at 0 into now (`created_at or int(time.time())`), so a valid event with created_at 0 fails verification.

Electrum's fork of aionostr: Event() recomputes the id and verifies the sig on construction. The wire id is never compared and cannot be: Event.from_json drops it ('we don't validate the original self.id, just always overwrite it') and the delivered Event holds only the recomputed one. Manager(connect_timeout=10) (default 5 s; bounds the untimed connect and the subscribe). Relay._receive_messages sleeps 5 ms before every message (CPU-DOS mitigation) and 5 s after any exception, and an event without a valid sig raises (ValueError 'missing sig'), so each of the 1547 unsigned events costs 5 s. get_events(filter_future_events_sec=None).
results.error: run 1: RunTimeout: no EOSE within 300000 ms

results.api: Client(Relay(url)).connect() + stream_events(client, Filter(limit)) async generator (ends at EOSE)
results.notes: bigbrotr/nostr-tools: Event.from_dict validates on construction (field formats, id recomputed, sig) and rejects empty tags and content/tags containing the text \u0000 (a literal backslash-u: the real U+0000 of the ambiguous event passes, while a valid kind 4550 event whose content is escaped JSON holding \u0000 is rejected); on failure it 'unescapes' content/tags and validates again, then stream_events logs the EventValidationError with a traceback (logger.exception) for every invalid event: formatted by logging's default last-resort handler, sent to /dev/null.

nostrclient does not verify received events; the harness builds nostrclient.event.Event from the dict, compares its id with the id field and calls verify() (sig against the id): two hashes per event, as Event.id is a property that recomputes on every access and verify() reads it again. Events reach the app through an emitter thread that drops events with no listener yet, so the app makes the Subscription, attaches its EVENT/EOSE listeners, then relay.subscribe(filter, sub=sub). Subscription dedups with a list (linear scan, reset at 10 000 ids). Each Relay starts a non-daemon emitter thread (0.1 s queue poll) that nothing stops: one more is left polling after every run.

results.api: read_events_from_relays([(url, websocket)], limit) -> deduplicated, sorted list
results.notes: connect_to_relays() cannot open a ws:// URL (it always passes ssl=, which websockets rejects), so the harness opens the websockets connection itself, as connect_to_relays does minus ssl (untimed). Fetch-only API, no verification of fetched events (its private _verify_event_signature is sig-only and used for NIP-17 seals); the harness verifies id (json.dumps compact, ensure_ascii=False, sha256) and sig (coincurve PublicKeyXOnly.verify).

nostrclient does not verify received events; the harness builds nostrclient.event.Event from the dict, compares its id with the id field and calls verify() (sig against the id): two hashes per event, as Event.id is a property that recomputes on every access and verify() reads it again. Events reach the app through an emitter thread that drops events with no listener yet, so the app makes the Subscription, attaches its EVENT/EOSE listeners, then relay.subscribe(filter, sub=sub). Subscription dedups with a list (linear scan, reset at 10 000 ids). Each Relay starts a non-daemon emitter thread (0.1 s queue poll) that nothing stops: one more is left polling after every run.

results.api: read_events_from_relays([(url, websocket)], limit) -> deduplicated, sorted list
results.notes: connect_to_relays() cannot open a ws:// URL (it always passes ssl=, which websockets rejects), so the harness opens the websockets connection itself, as connect_to_relays does minus ssl (untimed). Fetch-only API, no verification of fetched events (its private _verify_event_signature is sig-only and used for NIP-17 seals); the harness verifies id (json.dumps compact, ensure_ascii=False, sha256) and sig (coincurve PublicKeyXOnly.verify).
